::: {#rem-twice-fix}
#### One call instead of two

The function `dm` of @exr-twice-calls finds the same value $a_{n-1}$ twice.
Writing the recursive rule of @exm-doubling-sequence directly, with one recursive call,

```{racket}
#| code-fold: false
(define (dm1 n)
  (if (= n 0)
      2
      (- (* 2 (dm1 (- n 1))) 1)))
```

returns the same values, as the first six show:

```{racket}
#| code-fold: false
(map dm (range 6))
(map dm1 (range 6))
```

`(range 6)` is the list `'(0 1 2 3 4 5)`.
Each call of `dm1` makes only one recursive call, so its calls form a single chain instead of a tree that doubles at every level.
By @thm-twice-base-calls, `(dm 30)` makes more than a billion calls, since $2^{30} = 1073741824$.

:::
